scope: Standalone CPU/ABI verification of bounded draw-cache indexing and generic observer fast path; no game launch or FPS claim

cache_design.lookup: Expected O(1) hash indexes with bounded cardinality; capture-age and lineage links reside in stable nodes.
cache_design.admission: Do not evict entries already captured in this canonical frame. Reject excess admissions; evict older captures when needed.
cache_design.bytes: Vector capacities and conservative metadata/reference allowances are charged. This is retained CPU-data accounting, not process RSS or GPU/native image memory. A bounded in-progress capture is additional.
cache_design.no_op: Compact metadata, no state payload. Successful replay performs one exact lookup, no lineage lookup and no backend ReadState/ApplyState. Canonical entry/exit state checks remain.
cache_design.lineage: Queried on replay failure only; maintained incrementally through replacement/eviction.
cache_design.resources: Final per-image state selection is indexed, references remain retained until replacement/eviction/Clear on the existing game-thread path.
cache_design.native_effect_pool: Unchanged. 1024 native effect identities may yield more than 1024 draw-cache keys across passes.

cache_same_workload_benchmark.environment: Desktop WSL compiler, x86 Windows executable through interop, optimized MSVC ABI; single-run microbenchmark, not Steam Deck gameplay
cache_same_workload_benchmark.workload: 8 canonical capture sweeps; two full pure sweeps per canonical frame; unchanged no-op backend; native generation formula; 1024 entity identities with additional passes.
cache_same_workload_benchmark.measurement_note: This paired benchmark preceded only the capture-flag mirror addition; final integrated probe regressions below were rerun with that flag addition.

other_checks: Resetting canonical-frame history clears stale lineage
A single impossible-size entry does not evict unrelated old captures
A rejected replacement cannot replay its stale prior drawing
Existing deferred-vertex, final-resource, failure-restoration and unsafe-capture tests

observer_design.non_lazy_inactive: Push flags, compare a stable atomic capture byte, restore flags and jump to the same displaced-native/original target. No C++ Notify or FXSAVE/FXRSTOR.
observer_design.active: Restore incoming flags and execute the complete prior observer path.
observer_design.lazy: Always execute Notify, including outside capture, so frameUnsafe invalidation remains.
observer_design.lifetime: The flag lives in a retained gate allocation, not the Cache object. Begin/End/Clear mirror capture; Cache destruction sets it to zero.
observer_design.unchanged: Original native operations always execute. Specialized texture hooks and their lifetime tracking are not bypassed.

coverage: All GPRs including ESP and arithmetic EFLAGS
Real foreign thread forwards the native target without mutating capture reasons
Retired gate still calls native after Cache destruction
observer_tests.interpretation: The inactive path improves; active capture retains full observation and pays the added branch. This does not predict total game FPS.

limits: No isolated/live game was launched by this agent. Root owns exact-DLL gameplay performance and image/cadence regression.
Native update/render cost and actual graphics queries may remain bottlenecks.
Hash lookup is expected constant time, not an adversarial worst-case proof.
The native effect pool, Lua callback semantics, graphic dependency validation and unsupported-operation policy are not relaxed.
